conflicts.issue: FY23 County Funding Level for DPS ($9.88M Recommended vs. $12.875M Ask, Classified Wages, and School Nurse Funding)
conflicts.summary: DPS board members and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga pressed County leaders for greater funding beyond the County Manager's $9.88 million recommended increase to address classified wages ($16-$17/hour), teacher supplement competition, and school nurse funds, while County officials cited tax impacts and existing nurse vacancies.
conflicts.side_a_position: Increase local funding toward DPS's full ask, raise classified staff from $15/hr toward $16-$17/hr, and direct school nurse funds to address classroom/staffing needs.
side_a_arguments: DPS faces intense regional competition on teacher salary supplements and severe classified vacancies at the $15/hour wage floor (~$4M needed to reach $16-$17/hr).
Roughly $1.1 million funded previously for school health nurses stayed in County Public Health rather than coming directly to DPS.
Both boards need a multi-year funding plan and joint advocacy for state Leandro funding from the state's $6 billion rainy day fund.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold the recommended FY23 DPS increase at $9.88 million (8.97% general fund growth) and avoid additional property tax hikes while filling existing vacancies.
side_b_arguments: The $9.88 million increase matches general fund revenue growth and covers $5.3 million in state salary/benefit pass-throughs, plus mid-year nurse funding commitment once 10 existing vacancies are filled.
Residents already face inflation at the grocery store and an upcoming 2.5-cent tax impact if the 2022 school bond passes.
State lawmakers—who refused local school board taxing authority—must fund public education rather than relying solely on local property taxes.
conflicts.resolution: Informational joint budget discussion; no formal funding vote taken at the joint meeting.

meetings.title: BOCC/BOE Joint Quarterly Meeting | 11/29/22 | 9:00AM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners held their quarterly joint meeting the morning after certification of the $400 million 2022 education bond referendum. DPS staff presented the 10-year Capital Improvement Plan—detailing how the $400 million bond and Limited Obligation Bonds apply toward roughly $944M–$996M in capital needs, including Phase 1 renovations, Durham School of the Arts, Jordan High School site evaluation, and kitchen electrification. Board members and county budget officials discussed tracking bond-funded phases transparently for voters, future debt and bond cash-flow timing, and potential county uses for vacated school sites. Both boards also discussed rescheduling their February 2023 quarterly meeting to avoid conference and board-meeting conflicts before adjourning with no public speakers.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Bond Certification Remarks, and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the joint BOCC/BOE session and thanked County Commissioners and Durham voters following the previous evening's certification of the 2022 school bond referendum. Alexandra Valladares, participating remotely via Zoom due to illness, moved approval of the agenda, seconded by County Commissioner Heidi Carter.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 16, 2022 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The joint boards reviewed the minutes from their August 16, 2022 quarterly meeting. Jovonia Lewis moved and BOCC Chair Brenda Howerton seconded approval of the minutes.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) and 2022 Bond Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and Matthew Palmer presented the 10-year CIP priorities—expanding Pre-K and EC classrooms, modernizing aging schools, evaluating whether a new Jordan High School fits on its existing occupied site, advancing Phase 1 projects (six elementary renovations and Durham School of the Arts) to Construction Management at Risk in January 2023 and bidding in spring/summer 2023, and issuing Phase 2 RFQs in February–March 2023. Officials discussed applying the $400M bond and Limited Obligation Bonds toward the ~$944M–$996M plan, transitioning kitchens (e.g., Mangum) from gas to electric appliances, tracking bond-funded projects publicly, and coordinating future uses for vacated school land.

agenda_items.title: Draft 2023 Joint Quarterly Meeting Schedule and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and school board members noted that the proposed February 2023 joint meeting conflicted with a commissioner conference (Feb. 5–10) and a DPS board meeting, and asked clerks to evaluate January 31 or February 28 so the boards could meet ahead of the budget cycle. Chair Umstead noted no public comment speakers had signed up and adjourned the meeting.

meetings.title: Joint BOCC-Board of Education Meeting for August 16, 2022
meetings.executive_summary: BOCC Chair Brenda A. Howerton and DPS Board of Education Chair Bettina Umstead co-presided over the August 16, 2022 Joint BOCC-Board of Education Meeting, with all five County Commissioners present including Nida Allam. The joint body deferred a scheduled teacher housing update to the next meeting, corrected a typo and unanimously approved the May 10, 2022 joint minutes, and heard staff briefings on the November 8 $550.2 million General Obligation Bond Referendum timeline ($423.5M for DPS, $112.7M for Durham Tech, and $13.9M+ for the Museum of Life and Science at a projected 2.5-cent tax increase). DPS capital leadership reviewed active construction—including Lyons Farm Elementary's August 29 opening with October solar installation, the new Northern High School, and Murray-Massenburg Elementary—while debating the reuse of surplus school sites like old Northern High School and downtown DSA for affordable teacher housing. Child Care Services Association also reported Durham Pre-K had grown to 24 sites, 40 classrooms, and 607 locally funded seats, sparking discussion on South Durham expansion and DPS kindergarten-readiness data sharing.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Amendment (Teacher Housing Deferral), and Approval of May 10, 2022 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOCC Chair Brenda A. Howerton and BOE Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting and removed the DPS teacher housing item from the agenda because staff was not yet ready for a full update. Commissioners and BOE members then noted a minor typographical correction in the May 10, 2022 joint meeting minutes and approved them unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: 2022 General Obligation Bond Referendum Timeline and Blue Ribbon Committee Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager and Chief Communications Officer Deborah Craig-Ray outlined the $550+ million November 8 bond package ($423.5M DPS, $112.7M Durham Tech, $13.9M Museum of Life and Science; projected 2.5-cent tax rate impact), noting Local Government Commission approval in September, early voting starting October 20, and non-partisan factual voter education led by the Blue Ribbon Committee. Board members asked about LGC timing, property tax communication, and aligning DPS and County informational materials.

agenda_items.title: DPS Capital Projects Update and Surplus Site Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Chief Operating Officer Dr. Julius Monk, Construction Director Frederick Davis II, and Director Matthew Palmer updated both boards on Lyons Farm Elementary (opening August 29 with $3M solar installation slated for October), new Northern High School (topping-out ceremony held July 27 for 2023 opening), Murray-Massenburg Elementary (850 seats opening 2024), six elementary renovations adding Pre-K wings, and Durham School of the Arts planning. Officials discussed Safe Routes to School coordination, the 3-tier bus bell schedule, and repurposing soon-to-be-vacated campuses (old Northern High, 17-acre downtown DSA site, and Lowes Grove's ~73-unit teacher housing concept).

agenda_items.title: Durham Pre-K Enrollment, Funding, and Kindergarten Readiness Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Child Care Services Association leaders Katie Linder and Linda Chappelle reported that Durham Pre-K expanded from 16 sites/28 classrooms to 24 sites/40 classrooms and 607 locally funded seats backed by over $5 million in County investment, drawing 1,600+ applications and 778 acceptances while piloting ~40 wrap-care slots and $1,300/month BK-licensed classroom reimbursement rates. Commissioners and BOE members questioned South Durham site equity, dual-language programs, and executing a data-sharing agreement with DPS to track kindergarten outcomes.

votes.notes: Joint voice vote with Durham Public Schools Board of Education; all five BOCC members present during the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: After deferring the teacher housing agenda item by consensus and flagging a typographical error in the May 10, 2022 joint minutes, the two boards approved the corrected minutes unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: BOCC/BOE Joint Quarterly Meeting | May 10, 2022 | 9:00AM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over the May 10, 2022 in-person joint quarterly meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) and DPS Board of Education, which unanimously approved the agenda and February 15, 2022 minutes. DPS Building Services Director Frederick Davis and Dr. Julius Monk presented construction progress videos on Lyons Farm Elementary (on schedule and budget for August 2022) and the 2,000-student Northern High School, prompting intergovernmental discussion of unfunded off-site pedestrian/sidewalk improvements and County ARPA broadband investments ($10 million set aside). County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell presented her recommended FY23 budget featuring a $9.88 million (8.97%) funding increase for DPS totaling $176 million. In extensive Q&A, school board members and Dr. Mubenga pressed for higher local funding to raise classified wages above $15/hour toward $16-$17/hour, questioned $1.1 million in unspent Public Health school nurse funding, and urged joint Leandro advocacy, while County Manager Sowell and commissioners cited existing nurse vacancies and resident property tax strain alongside the proposed 2.5-cent bond tax impact.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and February 15, 2022 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the first in-person BOCC/BOE joint quarterly meeting in recent memory to order at 9:00 a.m. The joint boards unanimously approved the agenda by voice vote (seconded by Jovonia Lewis) and unanimously approved the February 15, 2022 joint meeting minutes (moved by BOCC Chair Howerton, seconded by Jovonia Lewis).

agenda_items.title: DPS Capital Projects Update: Lyons Farm Elementary and Northern High School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and Executive Director of Building Services Frederick Davis presented video recaps showing Lyons Farm Elementary on schedule and budget for August 2022 completion and structural/site progress at the new 2,000-student Northern High School. Officials discussed off-site sidewalk and American Tobacco Trail access needs not in the original project budget—recommending City of Durham participation—as well as $10 million in County ARPA broadband equity funds and state GREAT grants.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Recommended FY23 Budget Update and Joint Funding Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell outlined her recommended FY23 budget increasing DPS county funding by $9.88 million (matching the 8.97% general fund growth) to $176 million, including $5.3 million for state salary and health insurance increases and 3 new school health nurses alongside 10 unfilled positions. DPS leaders and board members (including Bettina Umstead and Matt Sears) raised concerns over the $1.1 million nurse allocation held in Public Health, regional teacher supplement competition, lifting $15/hour classified workers toward $16-$17/hour (~$4 million gap), and the need for multi-year planning and joint state Leandro advocacy, while County officials weighed tax pressures ahead of the 2022 bond.

votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; BOCC commissioners also participated in the joint voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead called for a motion to approve the joint meeting agenda. A member moved approval (mover name unclear in transcript audio), Jovonia Lewis seconded, and the joint boards approved the agenda unanimously by voice vote at 00:13:20.

meetings.title: Joint Board of County Commissioners and Board of Education Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs co-presided alongside Durham Public Schools (DPS) Board of Education Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis for the first joint BOCC–Board of Education meeting of 2022, with Commissioners Heidi Carter and Nida Allam attending while Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns were away at a conference. Both boards unanimously approved the November 16, 2021 joint meeting minutes before Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane presented the 10-year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) and roadmap toward a November 2022 General Obligation (GO) bond referendum covering DPS's $864 million 10-year facility request alongside Durham Tech, the Museum of Life and Science, and renewable energy. In the closing budget segment, Lane outlined the FY 2022-23 adoption calendar (Manager recommendation May 9, work sessions May 17–June 8, adoption June 13), BOE Vice Chair Lewis inquired about using $2.034 million in remaining ARPA ELC school-health funds, and commissioners and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga emphasized shared workforce retention challenges and future collaboration on Durham Pre-K.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of November 16, 2021 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Wallace called roll for both boards at 9:01 AM, noting BOCC members Wendy Jacobs, Heidi Carter, and Nida Allam were present (Howerton and Burns at a conference) alongside BOE members Lewis, Ravin, Beyer, Sears, and Valladares. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and BOE member Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the November 16, 2021 joint minutes, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: 10-Year CIP and November 2022 General Obligation Bond Referendum Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane presented plans for a November 2022 GO bond referendum addressing capital needs for DPS, Durham Technical Community College, the Museum of Life and Science, and renewable energy. Lane highlighted DPS's $864 million 10-year request driven by scope changes, Pre-K, class-size legislation, and inflation, and outlined key milestones: March CIP adoption, April market testing with voters, and a June 14 preliminary GO bond resolution.

agenda_items.title: FY 2022-23 Budget Calendar, ARPA School Health Funds, and Workforce Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane reviewed the FY 2022-23 budget schedule leading to a May 9 Manager recommendation and June 13 adoption, while BOE Vice Chair Lewis requested follow-up on whether DPS could access remaining ARPA ELC school health testing ($2 million) and reopening liaison ($34,000) funds. Commissioner Heidi Carter underscored balancing school investments with community safety and transit tax/rail priorities, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga thanked BOCC for its support, and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs praised staff vacancy/SWOT analyses and requested prioritizing Durham Pre-K at the next joint meeting before closing at 10:54 AM.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 16, 2021 Joint BOCC–Board of Education Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns were absent at a conference (3-0 BOCC aye). Seconded by DPS BOE member Natalie Beyer; BOE members Frederick Ravin, Natalie Beyer, and Matt Sears also voted aye and Vice Chair Jacobs declared the minutes unanimously approved.
votes.discussion_detail: Joint roll-call approval of the November 16, 2021 joint BOCC and DPS Board of Education meeting minutes.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOE/BOCC Quarterly Meeting February 15, 2022 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At the quarterly joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and DPS Board of Education—co-chaired by BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and DPS Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis with five DPS members present (Bettina Umstead and Dr. Mike Lee absent at a conference)—the two boards unanimously approved the November 16, 2021 joint minutes. County management committed to recommending full funding in the Capital Improvement Plan and upcoming 2022 General Obligation bond referendum for DPS's increased school construction and renovation scope (Elementary School F, new Northern and Jordan high schools, and DSA, Glenn, and E.K. Powe renovations), alongside a joint MWBE disparity study and renewable energy collaboration. DPS CFO Paul LeSieur also presented ESSER I-III spending (including three $1,500 retention bonuses) and previewed a $12.8 million preliminary FY 2022-23 local budget request plus $3.7 million if all classified pay is raised to $17/hour, while county staff presented their FY 2022-23 budget outlook.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Approval of November 16, 2021 Joint Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and DPS Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis co-chaired the virtual joint meeting with BOCC Commissioners Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Nimasheena Burns (joined later) and DPS Board Members Jovonia Lewis, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears, and Alexandra Valladares (Chairs Brenda Howerton and Bettina Umstead, and Dr. Mike Lee, absent). Moved by Commissioner Carter and seconded by Natalie Beyer, the November 16, 2021 joint minutes passed unanimously by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) and General Obligation (GO) Bond Referendum Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and County Budget Director Keith Lane outlined the CIP schedule (March adoption, April bond market testing, June 14 preliminary GO bond resolution) and stated county management would recommend fully funding DPS's cost increases driven by scope changes, pre-K class-size legislation, and construction inflation. Officials also highlighted solar-ready roofing and renewable energy bulk-buying opportunities following the BOCC's renewable energy plan adoption, plus a joint Durham County-DPS disparity study.

agenda_items.title: DPS Federal COVID Relief (ESSER) and FY 2022-23 Local Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS CFO Paul LeSieur reviewed $155 million in ESSER II/III allocations (including $34.4 million for HVAC/facilities, $25 million for summer learning, 23 mental health/school counselors, and $1,500 retention bonuses in November 2021, March 2022, and October 2022) and presented DPS's preliminary $12.8 million FY 2022-23 local request ($10.3 million DPS + $2.5 million charter pass-through) covering a $4 million teacher supplement increase to $6,500 starting, $17/hour bus driver pay, Lyons Farm staffing, and 7 IT technicians. Commissioners and board members discussed moving all classified workers toward $17/hour ($3.7 million additional cost), staff mental health, and whether federal ARPA/ESSER final rules barred aggregate affordable teacher housing.

agenda_items.title: Durham County FY 2022-23 Budget Process Update and Closing Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane reviewed county revenue projections, rising employee health insurance ($4.5-$5 million) and state retirement costs, departmental SWOT analyses, and key budget dates (May 9 manager recommendation, June 13 adoption). Joint members closed by emphasizing mental health investments, living wages, staffing retention, and scheduling a Durham Pre-K update for the next joint meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 16, 2021 Joint BOE/BOCC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: DPS Chair Bettina Umstead and Board Member Dr. Mike Lee were absent. BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs co-chaired with DPS Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis; BOCC Commissioners Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Wendy Jacobs also voted Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: In the joint BOE/BOCC roll call conducted by clerk Monica Wallace, BOCC Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and DPS Board Member Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the November 16, 2021 joint meeting minutes. All five present DPS members (Lewis, Ravin, Beyer, Sears, Valladares) and three present BOCC commissioners (Carter, Allam, Jacobs) voted Aye.
